title: Locals could see Northern Lights in the Valley
excerpt: The Northern Lights have been seen in the Valley this past summer, and local residents may have a chance to see them again.
content:
YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (WKBN) – The Northern Lights have been seen in the Valley this past summer, and local residents may have a chance to see them again.

A small blast of material from the sun’s outer atmosphere is expected to reach near Earth. This usually impacts magnetic fields and causes minor geomagnetic storms. As of right now, NASA is expecting the possibility of a G1 geomagnetic storm, which is the lowest and most common level of solar storm, representing a minor disturbance in Earth’s magnetic field.

This would cause the Northern Lights to potentially be visible again to most Northern states late Thursday into Friday morning. If it reaches G2, it would be possible again in the Valley. The only issue is that we may have a clear obstacle in the way: a cold front.

Right now, some clouds are trying to peel back due to a high-pressure influence to the Southeast. That will change, though, as the ridge of high pressure breaks down through the day. This will allow plenty of clouds to roll in throughout this evening, overall making it very difficult to see any type of light activity (even through your phone).

With that incoming front, clouds continue to thicken overnight. You’ll even have the chance of some small showers sneaking in toward early Friday morning.

Many states to the northwest of the Valley, like Montana, Minnesota and far North Michigan, will have a shot at seeing the Northern Lights. Our odds, though, aren’t so good due to our next impending weather system.
